originality.rationale: The optimization is strictly two-parameter, with a global equality classification and isotropic log-Hessian. Finch states only the regular value, Böröczky–Henk analyze regular polytopes, and Black–Criado give bounds for generic fixed-polytope shadows. A prior restricted axial parameter theorem and an available finite solid-angle formula do not imply the full triaxial extremum. The exact probability representation is supporting background, not a claimed novel mathematical fact. Residual risk: an older equivalent triaxial solid-angle extremum may be present in historical literature.
residual_risks: An equivalent all-triaxial optimizer may be implicit in older spherical-triangle or octahedral photography literature.
The exact general probability formula and restricted axial one-parameter case are already available background; only the sharp full three-axis extremum and log-shape Hessian are claimed as new.
Applied nanooctahedron literature could not be fully inspected and was not used to declare whole-document noncoverage.
A same-model scientific review is not independent validation.

value.rationale: All triaxial axis ratios are optimized sharply, resolving the natural expected vertex-count extremum for a two-modulus family of Euclidean cross-polytopes. Equality characterizes the regular configuration and the computed positive quadratic Hessian quantifies rigidity. Prior restricted one-axis optimization cannot exclude other local extrema in the second modulus. This is motivated by random-shadow combinatorial complexity rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
